corrected_verdict: KNOWN. The network-level identity is not just a "trivial extension" of the Morwani/Li single-neuron computation. It is a direct instance of a textbook result, the Poisson summation formula on Z_p^{n+1} (O'Donnell 2014, Sec. 3.3 and 8.5). Take H = {c = a_1+...+a_n}; its annihilator is H^perp = {(j,...,j,-j)}. Morwani App. F.3 already uses the network-level diagonal mode fhat(j,j,-j). Do not present eq:spectrum as a contribution.
issues:
I checked the math and every citation myself: I fetched the PDFs, and the ICLR and PMLR proceedings pages. I also ran a numerical check on a random real table (p=5, n=2); the identity holds to 1e-10.

The checker's verdict and both recommended citations hold up, with these corrections.

(1) Morwani pin-cites are imprecise.
- The eta~ identity is the unnumbered display just before Eq. (5) in App. F.1.
- Eq. (5) is the objective (2p/(p-1))(eta~(0) - E eta~). Eq. (6) is the summed form. The cosine/phase form is Eq. (7).
- So "\citet[App.~F.1, Eq.~(5)]" should read "App.~F.1" or "App.~F.1, Eqs.~(6)--(7)".
- The Theorem 7 proof outline does not repeat the identity. It states only the consequence E[psi'] = 2/((p-1)p^2) sum uhat vhat what(-j).

(2) Missed in-paper prior art: Morwani App. F.3.
- It defines the multidimensional DFT of the whole network function f(a,b,c).
- It uses the network-level diagonal mode: "when j = k = -l != 0, we must have fhat(j,k,l) > 0".
- So the network-level diagonal object is already in Morwani, not only in Li Lemma F.1.

(3) Missed textbook source.
- The checker asserted Poisson summation without fetching a source.
- O'Donnell, Analysis of Boolean Functions (CUP 2014; arXiv 2105.10386), Sec. 3.3, calls the Poisson Summation Formula "the following classical fact": E_{h~H}[f(h+z)] = sum_{gamma in H^perp} chi_gamma(z) fhat(gamma).
- Sec. 8.5 (p. 229) says these restriction notions "generalize easily to L^2(F_p^n)".
- With z = (0,...,0,-delta) this gives app:spectrum exactly. It is also the discrete projection-slice identity.

(4) Li et al. details.
- Def. D.5 is the power-neuron eta with (u1+...+uk)^k. The product-term eta~ and its formula p^{-(k+1)} sum what(-j) rho^{j delta} prod uhat_i(j) are inside the proof of Lemma D.7. Cite it as "proof of Lemma D.7".
- The appendix numbering comes from arXiv v4. The PMLR paper (258:523-531) is 9 pages.
- The venue is confirmed on proceedings.mlr.press/v258. The bib is correct; volume and pages could be added.

(5) Nanda and Gromov: I read the full PDFs; the checker had read only the abstracts.
- Nanda Sec. 4.2 fits the logits as sum_k alpha_k cos(w_k(a+b-c)) by OLS. I verified numerically that the OLS coefficient over the full table is exactly Re(beta_k). This could be a nice one-line remark connecting the paper's beta_j to Nanda's fitted quantity.
- Gromov Sec. 3.1, Eqs. (10)-(16), expands the constructed network's output. The (n+m-q) wave is "constructive interference"; every other term must "interfere destructively". This is the same signal-versus-interference language the paper uses. Cite it where "interference" is defined.
- Neither paper states the averaging identity.

(6) Adjacent prior art, not a scoop: Tian, NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv 2410.01779), Thm. 1.
- It writes the MSE loss of a quadratic net on an abelian group through network-level sum potentials r_{k1k2k}.
- Only the diagonal r_kkk couples to the target (the term -2 r_kkk). Off-diagonal terms are penalties, and Lemma 1 sets them to zero.
- This is the MSE analogue of the diagonal/interference split. It is optional related work.

(7) Doshi et al. "Grokking modular polynomials" (Eqs. 18-19) gives the n-operand construction-level cosine. It is not an identity. Mohamadi et al. 2024 has nothing relevant.

(8) Notation nit (confirmed): approach.tex writes conj(what(j)) and appendix.tex writes what(-j). They are equal for real w.

extra_citations.why: Textbook source for app:spectrum. Sec. 3.3, the 'Poisson Summation Formula' (a 'classical fact'), states E_{h~H}[f(h+z)] = sum_{gamma in H^perp} chi_gamma(z) fhat(gamma). Sec. 8.5 says it generalizes to F_p^n. Take H = {c = a_1+...+a_n} <= Z_p^{n+1}, whose annihilator is {(j,...,j,-j)}, and z = (0,...,0,-delta); this gives eq:spectrum exactly for an arbitrary logit table. The PDF title page confirms 'Originally published April 2014 by Cambridge University Press'.

Optional related work. Thm. 1 decomposes the MSE loss of a quadratic 2-layer net on abelian group multiplication into network-level Fourier 'sum potentials' r_{k1k2k}. Only the diagonal r_kkk couples to the target (-2 r_kkk); the off-diagonal ones are penalties that Lemma 1 sets to 0. This is the MSE analogue of the paper's diagonal-versus-interference split. The venue comes from the arXiv comments ('NeurIPS 2025 camera ready') and the PDF header ('39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)'); I did not fetch the NeurIPS proceedings page itself.
